In brief: the evidence supports treating "find the root cause" as premature. The two CS signals (rising tickets, falling adoption) cannot be assumed to be causes of churn rather than correlated symptoms (chain C2, HIGH), and whether the 4.1%→9.2% move is even a broad-based trend versus a handful of large accounts churning (chain C1, HIGH) has not been checked at all. Among four live candidate pictures — internal operational/product issue, sales-motion/ICP drift, external/competitive pressure, and statistical concentration — an internal cause is the best-supported working lead but is explicitly rated LOW confidence (chain C3) because three rivals remain genuinely unsettled. The recommendation (chain C4, HIGH) is to run a 2-3 week, low-cost diagnostic phase (customer-count/concentration pull, metric-definition check, release/staffing/cohort/competitive-timeline correlation) before committing any structural remediation spend, while running only safe renewal-outreach triage in parallel — overall Conclusion confidence LOW, by design, reflecting genuine unresolved ambiguity rather than a forced single answer.
